sentences: The dating app Hinge is testing a new feature and a cheaper subscription tier, its parent company Match Group stated during its Q3 earnings call yesterday.
Match Group has three categories of apps: Tinder , Hinge , and everything else (literally called Everyone Everywhere, and includes apps like OkCupid and the marriage-focused Upward ).
The 2026 Q3 earnings call focused on Tinder 's financial turnaround, with some metrics still declining, but with smaller dips than in previous quarters.

For example, daily active users were down one percent year over year in Q3, and monthly active users were down 5.5 percent, which is a one-point improvement from Q2, Match's supplemental materials state.
Tinder 's direct revenue in Q3 was $480 million, down two percent year over year.
And while Hinge brought in less than half of that revenue in Q3 — $221 million — that's a 19 percent increase from this time last year.
This is the other big story of Match's Q3 earnings: That Hinge continues to grow.
Monthly active users are up 12 percent year over year, and paying users are up 23 percent too.

Hinge has introduced several features this year, including the Signals heart to indicate "good dating behavior," Date Ideas to help plan something IRL, and Friend's Take , testimonials from loved ones on a dater's profile.

Additionally, Hinge is testing a lower-priced subscription tier, according to Match's Q3 earnings material, which is "designed to give users more choice and control through features like additional filters and custom location boundaries." Testing has apparently been resonating with women users.
The app plans on launching the tier by the end of 2026.
Anna Iovine is the associate editor of features at Mashable.
Previously, as the sex and relationships reporter, she covered topics ranging from dating apps to pelvic pain.
Before Mashable, Anna was a social editor at VICE and freelanced for publications such as Slate and the Columbia Journalism Review.
